lines.caption: This is a tour of the pull request for issue 157: renaming a file in place no longer crashes Thunar.
lines.say: This is a tour of the pull request for issue one fifty-seven: renaming a file in place no longer crashes Thunar.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
A rename starts on the main thread, from F2, the rename dialog, Properties, or undo and redo.
The job now keeps the file's location, read right there on the main thread.
On the worker thread, the job only renames the file on disk and gets its new location back.
It hands that to the main thread, and waits until the main thread is done.
The main thread points the file at its new location and reloads its details.
Then it tells the views, and the row redraws with the new name.
Back on the worker, the job records the old and new location for Ctrl+Z, and finishes.
lines.say: Back on the worker, the job records the old and new location for Control Z, and finishes.

lines.caption: On 26 November, Thunar crashed right after an in-place rename, reading a file's details that had already been freed.
lines.say: On November twenty-sixth, Thunar crashed right after an in-place rename, reading a file's details that had already been freed.

lines.caption: The rename job swapped those details in the background while the window drew the row; now the drawing thread swaps them.
Each file's details live in one shared object that nothing locks, so only the main thread, which reads it, may replace it.
Step 1: every rename except the bulk renamer starts this job, which now stores the file's location from the main thread.
Step 2: the worker renames the real file, and no longer swaps the details there, which was the cause of the crash.
Step 3: the hand-over blocks the worker until the main thread has run, so steps 4 and 5 finish before step 6.
Step 4: the swap happens on the thread that draws, so nothing can be drawing the row at that moment.
Step 5: as before, the folder hears about the rename and the views redraw the row.
Step 6: the undo entry is built from the old and new locations directly, and Ctrl+Z uses it to rename the file back.
lines.say: Step 6: the undo entry is built from the old and new locations directly, and Control Z uses it to rename the file back.

lines.caption: Before, the worker freed the old details and loaded new ones; a draw at that moment read freed memory.
Now the worker only renames on disk, and the main thread, which does all the drawing, swaps the details.
In the code, the worker calls GLib's rename, and the main-thread callback calls the new set renamed function.
lines.say: In the code, the worker calls G Lib's rename, and the main-thread callback calls the new set renamed function.

lines.caption: The bulk renamer already runs on the main thread, so its rename function is left as it is, for simpler upstream merges.
The PR changes the rename job, adds one function to the file code, and adds a test of 30 renames in a row.
To undo it, revert its one commit on main; it changes no settings or saved data.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It follows the issue's analysis, which put the crash on the main thread, reading freed file details.
Exo's source confirmed that the hand-over to the main thread makes the worker wait.
And Thunar's folder monitor already swaps a renamed file's details on the main thread.
The first commit was built and installed in the cloud container.
On that build, the smoke test passed twice, and the existing in-place rename test passed.
The new test first failed at rename 25 because the test lost a key press; Thunar did not crash.
lines.say: The new test first failed at rename twenty-five because the test lost a key press; Thunar did not crash.

lines.caption: After fixing the test, 30 renames in a row passed: Thunar kept running, and Ctrl+Z undid the last one.
lines.say: After fixing the test, thirty renames in a row passed: Thunar kept running, and Control Z undid the last one.

lines.caption: Reading exo's source showed the worker waits for the main thread.
The later review fix was only compiled here; CI builds and tests the pushed head.
Not run: the rename dialog, Properties and redo, and a memory-checking build that would catch the bug for certain.
The local code review at high found 6 things, fixed 1 and left 5.
The fix: the job now takes the file's location on the main thread, instead of reading it on the worker.
Left: an unconfirmed monitor case, and a short pause on slow network drives, as the monitor already has.
Also left: an unused option kept for upstream merges; the last two were this page and a ruled-out case.
CI's own review of each push is in the PR's code review comment.
CI's build, tests and review run on the first push, including the review fix not re-tested here.
Visual verify checks CI's screenshots once they exist.
Since the race depends on timing, only everyday use after the merge shows the crash is gone.
To see it yourself, open the issue, the branch's changes, and the PR's checks and CI comments.
Part 3. What comes later: nothing depends on issue 157.
lines.say: Part 3. What comes later: nothing depends on issue one fifty-seven.

lines.caption: This PR fixes the crash, and no open issue builds on it yet.
An unrelated GTK warning logged before the crash wasn't traced, and this PR leaves it alone.
lines.say: An unrelated G T K warning logged before the crash wasn't traced, and this PR leaves it alone.

lines.caption: In short: the rename job renames on disk, and the main thread updates the file, so drawing and renaming can't collide.
